title: From Regulation to Implementation: A Critical Evaluation of LLM-Assisted Regulatory Compliance in Industry
abstract: arXiv:2608.21317v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The European Union (EU) has emerged as a leading regulatory body in the development of sustainability and privacy regulations. While new regulation requirements vary, many include a documentation artifact to ensure compliance. Notably, the Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR) introduces Digital Product Passports (DPPs) for life cycle transparency, while the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) mandates Data Protection Impact Assessments (DPIAs) to mitigate privacy risks. Creating these compliance artifacts, however, is challenging. Industrial data, which often exists in heterogeneous formats and is scattered across company and supplier systems, is required for DPPs and can be difficult to extract into compliant DPP formatting. translated_title: 从监管到实施：对行业中大语言模型辅助合规性的批判性评估
translated_abstract: 欧盟（EU）已成为可持续发展和隐私法规制定领域的领先监管机构。虽然新的法规要求各不相同，但许多都包含确保合规性的文档工件。值得注意的是，《可持续产品生态设计法规》（ESPR）引入了数字产品护照（DPPs）以实现生命周期透明度，而《通用数据保护条例》（GDPR）则强制要求进行数据保护影响评估（DPIAs）以减轻隐私风险。然而，创建这些合规工件具有挑战性。工业数据通常以异构格式存在，分散在公司及供应商系统中，这是DPPs所需的数据，且难以提取为符合要求的DPP格式。此外，DPIA文档需要跨学科专业知识，且没有标准化格式，使得新系统的开发变得困难。为应对合规性的特殊复杂性...
tldr: 本文批判性评估了大语言模型在工业合规文档生成中的应用，指出其面临数据异构、格式标准化及跨学科知识整合等挑战，并提出改进路径。
en_tdlr: This paper critically evaluates the use of large language models in generating industrial compliance documents, highlighting challenges such as heterogeneous data, lack of standardized formats, and interdisciplinary knowledge integration, while proposing improvement pathways.
